cover.headline: A genuine engineering franchise, priced at its own median multiple while the sector de-rates
cover.lead: Sona Comstar makes differential gears and assemblies, starter motors, EV traction and suspension motors and, since Jun-2025, railway brakes and couplers, for 7 of the world's top-10 car makers and India's EV leaders. Q1FY27 was its best quarter (revenue +54%, BEV revenue +107% to 44% of automotive sales), and the 22-Jul-2026 DENSO joint ventures gave it a way into high-voltage and hybrid powertrains. The stock doubled in a year to ₹830 (74.1x trailing EPS). We forecast EPS of ₹12.01 / ₹14.28 / ₹16.94 for FY27-29E (+18% a year) at EBITDA margins in the lower half of the guided 23-25% band. The street values Sona on **P/E on one-year-forward EPS** (Jefferies 55x FY28E). The house multiple, its 53.3x forward-P/E median since mid-2022 cut by the 9.4% auto-component de-rating, is **48.5x Sep-28E EPS of ₹15.61 = {{dcf.tp|inr}} ({{dcf.upside|chg}}): we initiate with SELL.** Cross-checks: EV/EBITDA ₹710, DCF ₹310. Bull {{scen.bull.tp|inr}}; bear {{scen.bear.tp|inr}}.

arguments.h: The franchise is real: engineering, global share and the EV head start
arguments.p: 8.7% of the world's differential gears and 55-90% of India's; 19 products designed and scaled in-house in seven years (~₹1,800 cr of annualised revenue); 69 EV programmes with 36 customers; a ₹24,000 cr order book (5.4x revenue, 64% EV). DENSO will pay Sona royalties for its 2W/3W motor technology. Net cash ~₹1,000 cr.

arguments.h: But FY26 growth was bought and margins have stepped down
arguments.p: FY26 revenue +25%, but by our estimate the automotive business was flat: the railway purchase (₹1,643 cr) supplied the growth while BEV revenue fell 6%. The EBITDA margin fell from 27.4% (FY25) to 24.7% and 23.1% in Q1FY27 (company basis); the guided band has been cut twice (25-27% at the IPO, now 23-25%). ROE halved from 21% to 11% after the QIP.

arguments.h: Q1FY27 is a strong restart, and we model it
arguments.p: BEV revenue more than doubled and India, Europe and China grew. We model revenue +{{F.salesGrowth.0|n1}}% in FY27E, then +15% and +14%, margins of {{F.ebitdaMargin.0|pct}} → {{F.ebitdaMargin.2|pct}} (Screener basis) and EPS +17% / +19% / +19%. The DENSO deal (completion by Mar-2027) brings ~₹858 cr of cash and a 49% minority in the 2W/3W motor business: roughly EPS-neutral, so it is not in our numbers.

arguments.h: Valuation: the price is at the stock's own median while the sector is 9% below
arguments.p: At ₹830 Sona trades at 53.2x Sep-28E EPS, the same as its 53.3x forward median since Jun-2022 (we leave out the first year after listing, when it paid up to 117x). Auto-component peers were 9.4% below their five-year medians on 30-Sep-2026; the house rule applies that to Sona too. The call is narrow: we would be at HOLD below ~₹800. Robotics and physical AI (₹800 cr order book) is optionality management itself says matters only beyond three years.

catalysts: Q2FY27 results (due by mid-November 2026): whether commodity pass-through lifts the margin back towards 24% (company basis), and whether BEV revenue holds near Q1's record.
Completion of the DENSO share subscription in Sona eDrive (by 31-Mar-2027) and the incorporation of the HV joint venture (JV2); first JV2 customer nominations.
US EV demand and tariffs: the anchor EV customer's volumes and any India-US trade deal; the EU-India FTA.
Robotics and physical AI: start of production of the first of three orders (one "this quarter", the rest within 15 months).
Railway: HVAC and electric-panel orders, and any disclosure of the business's revenue and margin.

sections.title: Gears, motors and now railway brakes: a driveline and motor specialist for the world's car makers

blocks.p: Sona BLW Precision Forgings (brand: Sona Comstar) began in 1995 as a maker of precision-forged bevel gears for Indian cars and tractors. In 2019 it merged with Comstar Automotive Technologies (starter motors and alternators), listed in Jun-2021, and since then has moved into electric drivetrains. It reports one segment and does not split revenue by product. Its businesses are: **driveline** (differential gears, differential assemblies including the complete differentials that go into EV e-axles, intermediate and epicyclic gears, steering bevel boxes); **motors** (conventional and micro-hybrid starter motors; traction motors and controllers for electric 2- and 3-wheelers; suspension motors for an active-suspension system built with ClearMotion); **railway** (brakes, couplers, suspension and now HVAC and electric panels, bought from Escorts Kubota in Jun-2025); and **sensors and software** (NOVELIC, Serbia: mmWave radar). Robotics and physical AI was added as a vertical in Jul-2026.

sections.title: From a gear forge to a listed EV supplier, then a railway acquisition and a DENSO partnership

blocks.p: Three decisions explain most of Sona's growth from FY15 to FY25 (CEO, Q1FY27 call): adding product verticals (Comstar's motors, EV products), selling to the West (North America was 41% of FY25 revenue), and committing early to electrification (BEV share 2% in FY20, 36% in FY25). The former private-equity holding company, Singapore VII Topco III (the "erstwhile holding company" in the AR FY26), has exited; the Kapur family's Aureus Investment is now the only promoter (28%). Since FY25 the company has diversified away from the US EV programmes that drove it: a QIP in Sep-2024, the railway business in Jun-2025, and in Jul-2026 two DENSO joint ventures and a new robotics vertical ("Sona Comstar 2.0").

sections.title: Demand is healthy except in US EVs; costs and rare earths are the squeeze

blocks.p: Q1FY27 (call, 23-Jul-2026): demand healthy in all markets; India strongest (PV, CV and e-2W had their best quarters in Q4FY26; India 51% of Sona's FY26 revenue); Europe growing and electrifying (BEV, strong and plug-in hybrids); US EV sales weak (-16% in FY26, -28% YoY in Q4FY26) with a shift to hybrids; China mixed. OEMs are constrained by supply chains, not demand, in EVs.

bullets: **Electrification.** BEV share of Sona's automotive product revenue: 2% FY20, 25% FY22, 36% FY25, 35% FY26, 44% Q1FY27. Sona's EV content is in differential assemblies (any e-axle, any market), traction motors (Indian e-2W/3W) and soon high-voltage motors via the DENSO JV. Weakness at its anchor EV customer (not named) and a 16% fall in US BEV sales are what made FY26 a "tough" year.

**Hybrids.** North American and European OEMs are adding hybrids; Sona won a hybrid differential programme from a North American OEM in Q1FY27 (₹640 cr) and micro-hybrid starter motors are an established line. 20% of automotive revenue is hybrid / micro-hybrid.

**Costs.** Steel, aluminium, copper, freight, packaging and energy inflation since late 2025; pass-through to OEMs lags 1-2 quarters; Haryana minimum-wage rise from 1-Apr-2026; new labour codes from 21-Nov-2025 (one-off ₹30 cr provision).
**Rare earths.** China's heavy rare-earth magnet export curbs (from Apr-2025) remain; Sona has moved to light rare-earth alternatives and says it has no magnet shortage (Q1FY27 call).

**Railways.** Indian Railways capex ~₹2.9 lakh cr; brakes, couplers and suspension are safety-critical with long approval cycles; new HVAC (₹2,000-2,500 cr market) and electric panels (~₹1,500 cr) approvals in Q4FY26 (Q4FY26 call).

blocks.callout: **Why it matters:** Sona's growth depends less on vehicle volumes than on winning programmes and launching them on time. The order book gives visibility, but launches slip, volumes on EV programmes have repeatedly come in below plan, and the company itself discounts the order book. Margins depend on how quickly OEMs accept commodity pass-through.

sections.title: Driveline: the original franchise, still winning ICE, hybrid and EV programmes

blocks.p: Differential gears were Sona's first product and remain its foundation. A differential lets the driven wheels turn at different speeds in a corner; every car, truck, tractor and EV needs one per driven axle. Sona makes the gears (sold to axle and transmission makers) and, increasingly, complete differential assemblies, which carry more value per vehicle and go into EV e-axles made by OEMs and Tier-1s worldwide. It holds 8.7% of the global differential-gear market (CY25; 8.1% in CY23) and dominates India. Outside China it gained share in CY25. Margins are the company's highest: forging, machining and heat treatment are capital- and know-how-intensive, and programmes run for 7-10 years.

It keeps winning programmes in every powertrain, including ICE and hybrids, which reduces the dependence on BEV volumes. But its growth depends on programme launches 2-3 years out (most wins above start in FY28-29), and its share gains have slowed (8.8% in CY24, 8.7% in CY25).

sections.title: Motors: starters, EV traction and suspension motors, and a DENSO partnership that shares the upside

blocks.p: The motor business came with Comstar: starter motors for cars and trucks (4.2% of the global market) and micro-hybrid starters. Sona then built EV traction motors and controllers for electric 2- and 3-wheelers (now "almost 10% of revenue", ~25% of the Indian market) and a suspension motor for an active-suspension system (with ClearMotion; production ramping in China), the fastest-growing product in Q1FY27. Traction motors are the lowest-margin product: an assembled item with low value addition, and they dragged the Q1FY27 margin.

**The DENSO deal (22-Jul-2026).** Sona will move its 2W/3W EV business (air-cooled traction motors, inverters, e-axles; FY26 turnover ₹385.5 cr, net worth ₹347.1 cr) into a subsidiary, Sona eDrive, for ₹893.2 cr (₹857.5 cr in cash). DENSO subscribes for 49% of Sona eDrive at an enterprise value of ₹1,750 cr; Sona keeps 51% and control. Separately, a new JV for high-voltage, liquid-cooled traction motors and inverters for cars and trucks will be 51% DENSO and 49% Sona (Sona invests ₹26 cr initially). Each partner licenses technology to the JV it controls for a royalty. Completion is due by 31-Mar-2027.

sections.title: Railway: ~20% of FY27E revenue, lower margin, bought for ₹1,643 cr

blocks.p: On 1-Jun-2025 Sona bought the Railway Equipment Division of Escorts Kubota (brakes, couplers, suspension, air springs for locomotives, coaches, wagons and metros) for ₹1,643 cr in cash; it had ₹912.8 cr of revenue in FY25. Sona does not disclose its revenue or profit ("our job is not to help build better models", CEO, Q3FY26). From disclosed bounds we estimate ~₹900 cr in the ten months of FY26 (see the segments file) and ~₹1,107 cr in FY27E. The guided margin band fell a point when it was added, which implies an EBITDA margin around 20% versus ~25% for the rest: we use 20% rising to 21%, and ~25.4% for FY26 automotive.

bullets: **Growth levers (management):** demand above what is being supplied (capacity and supply-chain fixes), "white spaces" in existing product families, and new products: electric panels (~₹1,500 cr market, all rolling stock in 12-15 months) and HVAC (₹2,000-2,500 cr market, at least three years to cover all types). New products become meaningful "from the third year".

**Returns vs margins:** management says railway is "very high return" on its own capital though lower margin. On the ₹1,643 cr Sona paid (~1.8x FY25 revenue), the return is much lower: at ~₹1,080 cr of annual revenue and ~20% EBITDA, roughly ₹160 cr of pre-tax operating profit after depreciation and amortisation (our estimate), ~10% pre-tax on the price.
**Working capital:** railway customers pay slowly; group receivable days rose from 73 to 94 in FY26.

blocks.callout: **So what:** a sensible diversification away from US EV risk into a policy-backed Indian market, but it dilutes margins and, at the price paid, returns. It explains most of FY26's 25% revenue growth.

sections.title: Sensors, robotics and physical AI: a ₹800 cr order book and a long runway

blocks.p: NOVELIC (Serbia) gives Sona mmWave radar: in-cabin occupant sensing and a short-range exterior radar for an Indian commercial-vehicle OEM, aimed at upcoming Indian ADAS rules. In Jul-2026 management announced Robotics & Physical AI as a third growth engine with three orders worth ₹600 cr (an advanced robotics subsystem, a perception software stack for autonomous mobile robots, a radar perception solution), taking the vertical's order book to ₹800 cr; one order starts in Q2FY27, one in Q3 and one within 15 months. It is building its own AMR (shown at CES 2026) and plans cobots.

blocks.callout: **Our view:** this is where much of the 2026 re-rating came from (the stock rose ~16% from the Q1 results to 30-Sep), and it may become a real business: motors, gearboxes and sensors are robot building blocks. But management's own rule of thumb is "first three years no money, year 4 the first dollar, year 7-8 a $100 mn business", and it told investors that with a horizon under three years "none of this has any meaning". We give it no explicit value; it is part of what a 53.5x bull multiple would pay for.

blocks.callout: **Honest verdict:** A real but narrow moat: process know-how, cost and qualification lock-in on long programmes. It earns ~24% EBITDA margins and ~16% ROCE, good but not exceptional, and the share price discounts far more.

sections.title: Revenue up 2.8x in five years; margins have stepped down twice and EPS growth has slowed to single digits

blocks.p: Sona's consolidated revenue rose from ₹1,566 cr in FY21 to ₹4,449 cr in FY26 (Screener basis): 23% a year. The path had two phases. Up to FY24 growth was organic and fast (+36%, +25%, +20%) as EV differential assemblies, micro-hybrid starter motors and new customers ramped up, with EBITDA margins of 25-28%. FY25 slowed to +11% (US and European EV demand), and FY26's +25% came almost entirely from buying the railway business of Escorts Kubota (from 1-Jun-2025): by our estimate the automotive business was flat, BEV revenue fell 6% and the margin fell to 24.3%. EPS rose from ₹3.76 (FY21) to ₹10.29 (FY26), but only +10% and +6% in the last two years, because the ₹2,400 cr QIP of Sep-2024 added 5.6% to the share count and the cash it raised went into a lower-margin acquisition.

blocks.p: Sona has always spent heavily on capacity: capex of 10-16% of revenue in FY21-26 (Screener; FY26 includes ~₹110 cr of land for the railway business). Operating cash flow covered capex and dividends in every year since FY22. In Sep-2024 it raised ₹2,400 cr through a QIP (3.48 cr shares, ~5.6% dilution) with no immediate use; ₹1,643 cr of it went into the railway business in Jun-2025, and the NOVELIC stake was completed. ROCE on Screener's basis fell from 24% (FY24) to 14% (FY26) and ROE from 21% to 11%: the cash raised earns little until it is deployed, and the railway business, which management calls high-return on its own capital, was bought at ~1.8x revenue, so its returns on the purchase price are lower.

sections.title: Earnings quality: clean accounts and few one-offs; the weak spot is disclosure

bullets: **Cash conversion is good but slipped in FY26.** Cash from operations was 129% of net profit in FY25 and 103% in FY26 (₹659 cr) as receivables rose with the railway business; free cash flow after capex was ₹180 cr (Screener).

**Few one-offs.** Exceptional items were small after listing: a ₹30 cr after-tax labour-code provision in Q3FY26 (company adjusted PAT ₹670 cr vs reported ₹641 cr) and minor items in other years. The ₹233 cr gain in FY20 was before listing. We use reported EPS.

**Other income** (₹115 cr in the four quarters to Jun-26 before the labour-code charge) is treasury income plus forex gains; our FY27E ₹{{F.otherIncome.0|num}} cr sits between that and Q1 annualised (₹140 cr).

**Minorities:** NOVELIC's minority shareholders absorb part of its losses, so attributable profit is slightly above Screener's Net Profit row; we use attributable profit (EPS consistent with 62.2 cr shares).
**PLI income** (auto PLI scheme, eight approved products) is booked in operating income; Q4FY25 carried a full year of it, which flattered that quarter's margin by ~1.9 pts (Q4FY26 call).

**Disclosure:** no product or business-unit revenue, an order book that is a management estimate (10-year revenue, discounted), and margin claims for acquisitions ("~₹270 cr of profit at comparable margins") that cannot be checked.

blocks.callout: **Accounting flag: GREEN.** Walker Chandiok audit without qualification, few exceptional items, modest goodwill from the railway deal and genuine cash generation. Our caution is about disclosure (and therefore predictability), not accounting.

sections.title: Net cash ~₹1,000 cr after the railway purchase; working capital has stretched

blocks.p: At Mar-2026 Sona held ₹348 cr of cash and bank balances, ₹500 cr of current investments (debt funds) and ₹381 cr of fixed deposits, against ₹243 cr of debt (mostly short-term working-capital loans taken in FY26): net cash ₹1,026 cr on the company's basis, down from ₹2,659 cr a year earlier after the railway purchase. In our model the opening net treasury is ₹837 cr because Screener's borrowings also include ~₹199 cr of lease liabilities. Working capital stretched in FY26: receivable days rose to 94 and inventory days to 107 as the railway business (Indian Railways and wagon makers pay slowly) was consolidated; Q1FY27 brought a "significant reduction in debtor days" (CFO). Goodwill and intangibles from the railway deal sit in fixed assets (₹3,646 cr at Mar-26 vs ₹2,127 cr).

blocks.callout: **What you are buying:** one of the few Indian component makers with a global EV franchise: 8.7% of the world's differential gears, EV differentials and traction motors, 69 EV programmes, a ₹24,000 cr order book, a railway business that diversifies away from US EV risk, a DENSO partnership for high-voltage and hybrid powertrains, and net cash. **What you are paying:** 69.1x our FY27E and 58.1x FY28E EPS for ~18% a year EPS growth, ~23% EBITDA margins and an ROE that only reaches ~14% by FY29E. assumptions._revenueWhy: From the build below (Screener basis). FY27E: automotive and other non-rail +21% (Q1FY27 ex-railway ~Rs1,031 cr, +35% on a weak Q1FY26 when BEV fell; Q2-Q4 +22%, +15%, +12% as the base normalises; BEV +107% in Q1, 69 EV programmes, Rs24,000 cr order book = 5.4x revenue) plus a full year of railway (12 months vs 10: +23%).
